site.name: Semiconductor research desk
site.tagline: Value chain, quotes and research notes for 175 listed chip companies.
site.description: Eight value-chain stages, 13 headquarters regions and 175 listed companies, with dated quotes, published scoring rules and notes in four languages.

home.title: Follow the chip supply chain from EDA to packaging
home.lede: Quotes, structure and notes for 175 listed companies, from design tools to advanced packaging. Every number carries its date and source.

regime.title: Market state
regime.desc: Breadth, median 30-day return and dispersion across the 175 companies. It describes the market as it is, not as it will be.
regime.thresholds: Thresholds: expansion when breadth ≥ 60% and median return > 2%; contraction when breadth ≤ 40% and median return < -2%; otherwise neutral.

read.expansion: Most companies are up over 30 sessions. Check whether the move is broad or concentrated before acting on a screen.
read.neutral: About as many companies are down as up. Company evidence is more useful than a stage-wide call.
read.contraction: Most companies are down over 30 sessions. Check coverage before relying on any single screen.

chain.title: Value-chain structure
chain.desc: Company count, market cap and median 30-day return by stage. Equipment and materials are support layers, not steps in the flow.

movers.title: Momentum extremes
movers.desc: The five best and five worst 30-session returns among companies with a complete price history.

scatter.title: Valuation vs quality
scatter.desc: Each dot is a company: static P/E on the x-axis, ROE on the y-axis, market cap as area. Only companies with a positive P/E and complete fields.

watchlist.title: Research list
watchlist.desc: Three lists built from the published rules. They set reading order, not investment decisions.

news.title: Industry signals
news.desc: Headlines from five semiconductor publications, refreshed with every build.
news.empty: No usable headlines were retrieved in this build; the snapshot is shown instead.
news.sourceNote: Headline copyright remains with the original publisher.

knowledge.title: Knowledge base
knowledge.desc: Twelve notes on process, equipment, memory, policy and valuation, in four languages.

method.title: Method and boundaries
method.desc: Factor definitions, weights, thresholds and the limits of each number.

home.guideDesc: Six short tasks, a page-by-page answer table, and the conventions behind every number.

companies.title: Company map
companies.lede: Filter 175 companies by stage, headquarters and listing. Sort the table, open a profile, or compare within a stage.
companies.metricsNote: P/E is static (last annual EPS), P/B is book value, ROE is return on equity, and market cap is converted to USD at the snapshot rate.

company.dataNote: Quotes come from public market APIs and may be delayed. Missing fields show as —; coverage measures completeness, not accuracy.
company.unpriced: No verified quote source is available for this company. The research entry is kept, but it is excluded from quote statistics.
company.positioningTemplate: {name} works in the {stage} stage as a {role} company. Its capabilities cover {products}.
company.priorityDesc: Each factor is a percentile within peers; missing factors are renormalised.

chain.title: The value chain
chain.lede: Eight stages: six in the main flow, plus equipment and materials. For each one, how it earns money, which metrics matter, and who competes in it.
chain.note: Stages follow the primary revenue source. A company that both designs and manufactures is counted once, in its main stage.

knowledge.title: Knowledge base
knowledge.lede: Industry notes organised by theme. Each one stands alone and links to the companies and terms it uses.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lede: Semiconductor terms with Chinese, English, Japanese and German definitions, so the same word means the same thing across markets.

method.title: Method
method.lede: Every number on the site comes from a rule on this page.
method.purpose: Three questions in one sitting: what state is this stage in, which companies are worth reading first, and is the data behind that judgement complete?
method.not: No buy or sell calls, no price targets, no position sizing, no earnings forecasts. Missing data is shown empty rather than filled in.
method.universe: 175 listed semiconductor companies, each assigned to one of eight stages by primary revenue source, with one primary listing to avoid double counting.
method.factors: Percentile ranks within each stage, scaled 0-100, then weighted into a research priority. Stages with fewer than eight companies fall back to the full sample.
method.factorValue: Inverse percentile of static P/E; P/E ≤ 0 is treated as missing and the remaining weights are renormalised.
method.factorMomentum: 60% × percentile of 30-session return + 40% × percentile of 52-week range position.
method.factorSize: Percentile of log market cap in USD, a proxy for liquidity and resilience.
method.scoreFormula: Research priority = 0.30 × quality + 0.25 × valuation + 0.25 × momentum + 0.20 × size
method.confidence: Coverage is the share of eight fields present: price, 1D, 30D, market cap, P/E, P/B, ROE and 52-week range. 87.5% or more is high, 62.5% or more medium, below that low.
method.regime: Breadth, median 30-day return and dispersion, with fixed thresholds published above so any call can be checked later.
method.limits: Quotes are delayed or at the close. Static P/E penalises fast-growing companies. Revenue growth and order data are missing. Stage assignment involves editorial judgement, and currency conversion uses one daily rate.
method.disclaimer: For industry research and learning. Data can be delayed or wrong; the exchange filing is the authority.

about.title: About
about.lede: Public data, published rules, and the code that produces both.
about.mission: Semiconductors combine hard technology, long cycles and export policy. This site keeps the value chain, company positions and market data in one place, and shows the rule behind each number.
about.audience: Students and researchers learning the value chain, analysts and practitioners who need a fast global view, and individual investors who want transparent data definitions.
about.scope: 8 value-chain stages, 13 headquarters regions and 175 listed companies across mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, the US, Japan, Korea, Europe and Israel.
about.sources: Quotes, valuation and 52-week ranges come from the Eastmoney public quote API; FX from open.er-api.com; headlines from publisher RSS. Everything is written into a snapshot at build time, and pages never call a third-party API.
about.cadence: Rebuilds every 20 minutes while Shanghai or New York is trading, a pre-open pass at 08:30 Beijing time, weekly anomaly review and a monthly universe review.
about.license: Code is MIT licensed, written content is CC BY 4.0, and market data remains the property of its providers. Cite SiliconScope with the access date.
about.contribute: Data corrections, glossary additions and documentation improvements are welcome. Include a verifiable source and state the scope of impact.
about.disclaimer: No investment advice, target prices or return promises. Decisions based on this content are the reader's own.

guide.title: How to use the site
guide.lede: What you can actually do here, and what each number means.
guide.convTimeDesc: The snapshot time is shown in the header, footer and status page. Quotes may be delayed or at the close.
guide.convCoverageDesc: Low coverage means missing fields, shown as —. It is not a hidden opinion.
guide.convColorDesc: Up is teal with a plus, down is copper with a minus. Colour is secondary; the sign carries the meaning.
guide.convScoreDesc: The priority score orders reading. It is not a recommendation, target price or forecast.

tasks.title: Learn the chain
steps: Read the value chain once, from EDA to packaging.
Open one process you care about, such as lithography or packaging.
Look up unfamiliar terms in the glossary.

tasks.title: Find a company
steps: Press ⌘K and type a name or ticker.
Open the result, or use the search box on the company map.
Filters stay in the URL, so the link can be shared.

tasks.title: Compare one stage
steps: Choose a stage and, if needed, a country.
Open a company and use the peer table at the bottom of the page.

tasks.title: Read a company in two minutes
steps: Start with the positioning line at the top.
Check the 30-session chart and the 52-week range.
Read the priority breakdown and data coverage before trusting the score.

tasks.title: Verify freshness
steps: Click the health chip in the header.
Check data age, coverage and unpriced names.
Read the data notes before using a number in your own work.

tasks.title: Track the market
steps: Read the market-state card and the one-paragraph summary.
Look at the three research lists and the leading/lagging stages.
Open the method page if a rule is unclear.

faq.a: No verified quote source is available. The company stays in the universe for research, but its price is excluded from market statistics.

faq.q: Why did a priority score change?
faq.a: Percentiles are recalculated on every build. A new quote, a missing field or a peer moving can change the rank even when the company has not changed.
No. Scores order reading; they are not recommendations, target prices or forecasts.

faq.q: How often is the data updated?
faq.a: Once per trading day at 08:30 Asia/Shanghai. The exact snapshot time is on the status page and in the footer.
Some listings have no reliable quote or missing fundamentals. Missing values show as — and are never estimated.

status.title: Data status
status.lede: How fresh the data is, what is missing, and how the site is maintained.
status.cadenceText: GitHub Actions rebuilds the snapshot every 20 minutes while Shanghai or New York is trading, plus a pre-open pass at 08:30 Beijing time. Open pages refresh their quotes within a minute. A failed fetch falls back to the last snapshot and is marked stale.
status.runbookText: Failure handling, service levels and change management are documented in OPERATIONS.
